response.sql: SELECT m.college, SUM(i.amount) AS total_income, CAST(SUM(i.amount) AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM income) AS fraction_of_total_income FROM income i JOIN member mb ON i.link_to_member = mb.member_id JOIN major m ON mb.link_to_major = m.major_id GROUP BY m.college;

assumptions.assumption: The database is SQLite, so CAST(... AS REAL) forces a real-valued division, and the division yields NULL if total income is zero.
Inner joins drop income whose link_to_member has no matching member and members whose link_to_major has no matching major. A major with a NULL college would form its own NULL group in the output.
The denominator is the sum of amount over every income row, including rows with no member or major link. NULL amounts are ignored by SUM.
The fraction is left unrounded, as the request specifies, so it appears as a full-precision REAL.
